PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); this package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), no hardware was attached, no hardware or MuJoCo-engine run is claimed, no network or pip was used, and the read-only clone was not modified. ENTRY: the card's sim2sim.sim2sim:run_mujoco exists at sim2sim/sim2sim.py:53. It is a MuJoCo sim-to-sim loop that reads a YAML config, loads an MJCF with mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path (sim2sim.py:90), loads a TorchScript policy, writes PD torques to data.ctrl (sim2sim.py:159-161) and calls mujoco.mj_step (sim2sim.py:163); it exposes no reset/step/seed and imports the Isaac Gym training package and a keyboard listener, so this package serves the model through the card's family-config/MujocoDriver decision instead of importing or running the script. No helper deviation. MODEL: the package serves the card's models[1], resources/robots/N2/mjcf/n2_18dof.xml, because the README's sim2sim procedure tells the user to update sim2sim/configs/n2_18dof.yaml (README.md:59) and that config selects this file (n2_18dof.yaml:3); the script's own __main__ default is n2_10dof.yaml (sim2sim.py:176), an inconsistency of the clone, and the card's models[0] N2_10dof.xml is therefore not the served file. The loaded model has a free base (7 qpos, 6 qvel) and 18 limited hinge joints (18 qpos, 18 qvel), so the world state has 25 qpos and 24 qvel values, and 18 motor actuators. cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action: {ctrl: [18 numbers]}}; cap.world.reset.v1 runs mj_resetData + mj_forward and restores the parsed model defaults; the state is the bridge integration state. NO CONTROL LIMIT: the motor actuators declare no ctrlrange or ctrllimited (n2_18dof.xml:169-191), so the bridge derives no actuator_ctrlrange and the driver declares no control envelope; no bound was invented or copied from a catalogue or constructor default. The joint ranges (n2_18dof.xml:52-156) are MuJoCo joint position limits, not control bounds. No site-limits.example.json is needed and there is no operator-required limit. TIMESTEP: the MJCF states no <option timestep>; the fake uses MuJoCo's 2 ms default, which is also the upstream config's simulation_dt 0.002 s (n2_18dof.yaml:8) that run_mujoco writes into model.opt.timestep (sim2sim.py:91). FAKE: MuJoCo is not installed and cannot be installed where the gate runs, so backends['fake'] is fake.py, a stand-in mujoco module. It parses the same MJCF for the free base, the 18 hinge joints, the 18 motors and the option timestep, but integrates a placeholder velocity proportional to each control value and holds the free base fixed; it loads no STL mesh, resolves no contact, inertia, gravity, constraint, damping or actuator dynamics, reads no foot-force or IMU sensor, and was not compared with MuJoCo. The fidelity gaps list every difference. The real mujoco path (a backend name backends does not list) was not run. EXPECTED WARNINGS from the last gate run, all explained and none failing: G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND (the fake is a stand-in library object, not the upstream simulator, so native calls are not recorded and G7 has no fake surface); G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE (no limit on any actuating capability, so SAFE-014 has nothing to probe; the suite awards CL2 for that test and every other CL3 test passed); and G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the bridge-derived inputs ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised. TESTS: test_driver.py keeps the required mhs.testing.check_driver(HERE, backend='fake') call and adds nine cases (model shape from the served model, control-vector length, no invented control range, an observable step, reset to the model defaults, reset seed accepted without changing the model, published fidelity contract, e-stop latch); they pass within the gate's [...]
